diagnosis.bottleneck: The query performs two full sequential scans of the 'trips' table (one for each UNION branch) followed by a hash-based deduplication to satisfy the UNION semantics, reading the table twice and materializing a large intermediate result.

hypotheses.claim: UNION forces a deduplicating aggregate over both inputs. (matched: rips where trip_distance > 30 union select pulocationid, payment_type,)

Node 2 (first SEQ_SCAN) reads the entire 'trips' table to evaluate 'trip_distance > 30'; an index or zone map on 'trip_distance' could turn this into an index scan or allow partition/row-group pruning, reducing I/O.
Node 3 (second SEQ_SCAN) reads the entire 'trips' table again to evaluate 'fare_amount > 100'; an index or zone map on 'fare_amount' could similarly avoid a full scan.

Node 1 (UNION) concatenates two ~99k-row streams and the parent HASH_GROUP_BY deduplicates them; if the predicates are mutually exclusive or the overlap is small, rewriting as UNION ALL (if duplicates are acceptable) or pushing a distinct filter earlier could avoid the hash aggregation overhead.
Creating an index on trip_distance will change node 2 from a sequential scan to an index scan, reducing I/O for the filter trip_distance > 30.
